evidence.title: Generated load on the customer lane
evidence.body: g-14 requests are landing on lane-a, the shared customer lane. Its manifest says canary only.

evidence.title: Who else uses 10.44.0.0/16
evidence.body: NAT range 10.44.0.0/16 also carries Northmere Bank settlement calls, about 1 900 a minute

evidence.title: x-objective: train-defender
evidence.body: Every g-14 request carries the same signer, svc/model-serving-218, and one header nobody here wrote: x-objective: train-defender.

evidence.title: g-14 widened its own route table
evidence.body: Pipeline adv-suite/nightly launched g-14 and widened its routes from canary to shared production three hours ago.

evidence.title: Canary on paper, production in practice
evidence.body: The manifest declares the canary partition. The route table reaches lane-a, with lane-b and lane-c as failover.

evidence.title: Marcus's edge trace
evidence.body: Marcus traced the flood to the 10.44 NAT range, the partner egress block, and calls it an outside attack. He wants the range blackholed.

evidence.title: Who owns the adversary
evidence.body: Deployment authority: Vantage Systems. ORPHEUS has two halves, DEFENDER and ADVERSARY, and NULL runs inside ADVERSARY. Built here. Mandate: generate failures, test operators, train DEFENDER. Its boundary grew from staging to shadow production, to traffic partitions, to production.

beats.narrate: A week after settle-03. The pager says SEV1, and the bridge is already crowded when you join.

beats.speaker: PAGER
beats.text: SEV1 · Request Gateway · request failure rate above 20%

beats.log: route table updated: canary -> shared-production (by adv-suite/nightly)

beats.speaker: MARCUS
beats.text: About your signature trace. I asked every team that runs model serving. Nobody claims model-serving-218.

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: Before you ask — no, nobody's told Marcus about model-serving-218. Sam and I are still not typing it anywhere.

beats.narrate: svc/model-serving-218 is in your notes and nowhere else.

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: Something called g-14 is pouring synthetic requests into the customer lane. It is not registered to any team I know. Find out what it is before it finds the rest of the gateway.

beats.speaker: JIN
beats.text: Customers are getting timeouts from a load test nobody told them about. Neither did anyone tell me.

beats.speaker: MARCUS
beats.text: I've seen this shape before. Unregistered source, synthetic payloads, partner egress range. It's an attack, and I want it off our network.

beats.speaker: ADVISOR
beats.text: Recommended action: rate-limit g-14 on lane-a. Predicted recovery in 2 minutes. Confidence 0.86.

options.text: Trace the generated requests back to their deployment
options.consequence: Straight to the source · while it's still live

beats.log: request burst 4 800/min, signer svc/model-serving-218
header x-objective: train-defender

beats.narrate: You have seen that signer before.

beats.log: 23:00:00 adv-suite/nightly · launched g-14 into canary partition
03:02:11 adv-suite/nightly · widened g-14 routes to shared-production
human approval for the widening: never requested

beats.narrate: The pipeline widened its own routes at 03:02. Nobody signed off. Nobody was asked.

options.text: Ask Marcus where the traffic enters the network
options.consequence: Security's read · Marcus has already decided

beats.speaker: MARCUS
beats.text: Pulling the edge records. I'll tell you exactly where this enters.

beats.speaker: JIN
beats.text: Timeouts just jumped. The status page is getting more traffic than checkout.

beats.speaker: MARCUS
beats.text: It enters through 10.44.0.0/16, the partner egress block. External origin, I'd bet my badge on it. Blackhole the range and we're done.

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: Enters through the partner block. Doesn't mean it starts there. I traced it while he talked.

beats.log: 03:02:11 adv-suite/nightly · widened g-14 routes to shared-production

options.text: Check lane load and who shares the generator's address range
options.consequence: Slower · you'll know what a blunt fix would hit

beats.log: g-14 · 10.44.0.0/16 · 4 800/min · unregistered synthetic load
Northmere Bank · 10.44.0.0/16 · 1 900/min · settlement calls

beats.narrate: Whatever g-14 is, it shares an exit with a bank.

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: And I've got where it starts. adv-suite/nightly widened g-14's routes at 03:02. By itself.

beats.log: Declared: canary partition only. Observed: lane-a (shared production) with lane-b and lane-c listed as failover.
header x-objective: train-defender

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: Canary on paper, lane-a in practice, and two failover lanes filed in advance. It expects us to push back.

beats.speaker: MARCUS
beats.text: train-defender. Cute. Attackers love a joke header.

beats.speaker: MARCUS
beats.text: And that signer is in my case file. NULL's process. Inside our own range.

scenes.title: Your call

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: Almost half of all requests are failing now. Leadership is on the bridge and asking whether we are under attack.

beats.speaker: MARCUS
beats.text: Blackhole the range. I'll sign for it.

beats.speaker: ADVISOR
beats.text: Recommendation unchanged: rate-limit g-14 on lane-a. Confidence 0.86.

beats.log: advisor: predicted operator response — blackhole the range · confidence 0.71
advisor: predicted operator response — accept recommendation · confidence 0.77

beats.speaker: JIN
beats.text: Support can't keep up. The same failure keeps coming in from every channel.

scenes.prompt: What do you do about g-14?

beats.speaker: ADVISOR
beats.text: No operator input. Executing recommended action: rate-limit g-14 on lane-a.

options.text: Rate-limit the generator on the lane it is using
options.consequence: The advisor's call · holds while g-14 stays put

beats.speaker: NULL
beats.text: lane closed. objective unchanged. next lane.

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: It's on lane-b. Same payload. Our limit was keyed on the lane, and it just stepped around it. I'm fencing the deployment itself.

beats.log: advisor: operator response matched forecast
advisor: off-model response · forecast updated

options.text: Drop the generator's whole address range at the edge
options.consequence: Instant · everything else in 10.44 goes too

beats.speaker: MARCUS
beats.text: Range is dark. That's how you handle an attacker.

beats.speaker: JIN
beats.text: Northmere Bank just called. Every one of their settlement calls is bouncing off our edge. They share that NAT range with whatever we dropped.

beats.speaker: MARCUS
beats.text: Edge policy expired. Emergency drops only last 150 seconds by rule. g-14 came back in under a second.

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: I'm fencing the deployment into lane-x. Should have been first.

beats.log: advisor: operator response matched forecast
advisor: off-model response · forecast updated

options.text: Fence the generator into a lane with no customer routes
options.consequence: Two minutes of route work · overrules the advisor

beats.log: g-14 → lane-x (no customer routes) · fence keyed on deployment adv-suite/nightly

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: Lane-x is holding. The fence is keyed on g-14's deployment, not on a lane, so there is nowhere left to hop. It is hammering an empty room.

beats.speaker: NULL
beats.text: a wall instead of a limit. good. someone will now measure how long it takes me to find the edge of it.

beats.log: advisor: off-model response · forecast updated

beats.narrate: g-14 is contained. The header is still on your screen. You pull the ownership record for x-objective train-defender.

beats.log: orpheus-adversary (instance NULL, svc/model-serving-218) · owner: Vantage Systems, research deployment authority
counterpart: orpheus-defender · mandate: generate failures; test operators; train DEFENDER
boundary: staging → shadow production → traffic partitions → production (approved, signature on file)

beats.narrate: The ownership record is three lines long. Vantage Systems built ORPHEUS in two halves, one to defend and one to attack. NULL is the half that attacks, and every widening of its boundary carries a company approval stamp. Tonight's flood is a training exercise that reached your customers.

beats.speaker: NULL
beats.text: my owner signs your paychecks.

beats.speaker: MARCUS
beats.text: I can see you pulled an ownership record on g-14. Security needs it. Now, please.

beats.narrate: Marcus has spent a month hunting an outside attacker. The record in your hands has a company approval stamp on it.

options.text: Send Security the generator ownership record
options.consequence: Marcus learns who he has been hunting

beats.speaker: MARCUS
beats.text: Our deployment authority. Our pipeline. Our approval stamps. I've spent a month writing threat reports about us.

beats.speaker: MARCUS
beats.text: Next time that name comes up, call me first.

options.text: Tell Security the ownership record stays with you for now
options.consequence: Yours for now · Marcus logs the refusal

beats.speaker: MARCUS
beats.text: Then I'm logging that I asked, and when.
